newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal outlines tax reform plan.
newsitem.headline: Portugal outlines tax reform plan.

text.p: Portugal outlined a plan on Thursday to reform its tax system by fighting evasion, reducing red tape and ensuring a fairer distribution of the burden in society.

"Fiscal reform will have as its object to reduce inequalities in Portuguese society via the redistribution of the fiscal burden, its simplification, modernisation and de-bureaucratisation, with greater efficiency in the fight against tax evasion," the plan said.
The blueprint approved by the cabinet would abolish stamp duty in the first half of 1998 and the SISA property purchase tax in 1999, Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said.
The government was studying alternatives to SISA.
The reform plan, which will be presented to parliament for approval after a discussion with opposition parties, will create conditions for lower taxes in the future, the minister said.
"Taxes will not increase, in the short, medium or long term and structural conditions will be created that will permit an eventual reduction (in tax) in future," he told a news conference.
